title: Kobi <> Cedrick - Daily Standup - 2026/08/19 10:30 EDT - Notes by Gemini

items.topic: Pivot from storage proofs to CMS integration
items.statement: Jumpr will move the build focus from the storage proof story to the CMS integration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So, I I think you you saw the message yesterday. So, we it sounds like we are going to be pivoting from the uh the storage proof story to the CMS integration instead.

items.topic: Storage proofs on hold pending client
items.statement: After a meeting the day before, the client wanted to do internal work first on storage proofs and then come back to Jumpr; the timing is unknown.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um they like we basically met them yesterday and they wanted to uh do some additional like work internally first and then get back to us. So, I don't know when that's going to be.
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee.

items.topic: CMS integration blocks go-live; endpoints pending
items.statement: Kobi says the CMS integration is a big blocker for go-live, and Jumpr still waits for endpoints and information from the client.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: That's going to be like a big blocker for us to go live. Um, we're still waiting on endpoints uh and information from them,

items.topic: Data model work started before endpoints
items.statement: The proposal is to build the data model on the Jumpr side first so work can run in parallel until client endpoints are ready; Kobi says a lot of that work has already started.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: it seems that um your proposal is that we would um start the development of uh of the of the data model first on our end. / Cedrick Infantado: So so that they we could work simultaneously when um when the endpoint on their end is already unblock. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yes. So, actually we we started a lot of that work already.

items.topic: Deal is unique operator-partner-market-country-vertical combination
items.statement: In Salesforce a deal is a record that is a unique combination of operator, partner, market, country and vertical.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So in Salesforce it's yeah like it's like a unique combination of operator partner market country and vertical. That's what a deal is.
items.note: Restatement of the current design in an internal walkthrough; no client attendee.

items.topic: Deal rep assignment moves to CMS
items.statement: The client wants to do deal rep assignment in its CMS, not in Salesforce. Jumpr first proposed doing all assignments in Salesforce and sending them to the CMS, but the client already has a CMS interface for it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: this is the this is the interface that we've built so far, but they actually want to do the deal rep assignment in in their CMS as you'll see in the document. Uh, so they're not going to necessarily do the assignments in Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Initially we were proposing you know do everything in Salesforce like even the assignments and send it to CMS but for them it was uh easier to because they already have like a interface for the CMS.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier Jumpr proposal: do deal rep assignments in Salesforce and send them to the CMS. Now: assignments done in the CMS and synced back to Salesforce.
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee.

items.topic: Links built in Salesforce, sent to CMS
items.statement: Ops create deal records and add links in Salesforce; links are sent to the CMS, where links are activated or allocated to reps; the resulting assignments (DRAs) come back to Salesforce so both systems stay in sync and reporting runs from Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh, no. So, they're going to set up the links in Salesforce and send the links to uh the CMS and uh CMS is how they're going to allocate those links to the / Cedrick Infantado: So, the assignment would really happen on the CMS and then it would just sync up this in Salesforce set. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm going to add the links for the deals and then what we need is those to get sent to the CMS. That should enable the the person to activate those links or associate them to reps uh which then come back to us as rep uh DRAs or assignments and then we're just trying to keep both systems in sync so that
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee.

items.topic: Multiple capped links per deal
items.statement: A deal can have any number of affiliate links; each link has a cap on associated sign-ups, links can be shared or one per rep, and links are activated or deactivated from the deal in Salesforce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Like uh this is going to be like a affiliate link for this particular deal. And they could have more than one um any number and then each link could have uh the number of sign up or the number of uh people that can be associated to this link. Um so in a lot of cases one link is for one rep. Um but in some cases a rep can share the same link or in other cases they can have multiple links. So this that they have like a cap and then they want to uh activate or deactivate the uh links from here
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee. Based on the client mockup shown on screen.

items.topic: Assignment details visible in Salesforce
items.statement: Assignments synced from the CMS should show in Salesforce which rep has the deal, whether it is selective, and start and end dates; the layout needs cleanup.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh well, we'll need to clean up that layout, but we'll we'll be able to see like which rep is assigned to the deal. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Is are they selective? Is it uh what are the start and end dates and things like that? We should be able to see from the Salesforce side.

items.topic: SLC records convert to sign-ups
items.statement: Study link clicks from the CMS are created as SLC records (player, link, click time) and converted into sign-up records once mapped to the right deal and deal rep association.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: those link clicks that they do here get created as uh SLC records. So SLC records are study link clicks um which is the data that comes from the CMS on / Kobi Kunasekaran: who the player is um what what link did they click when did they click it and all that stuff which then gets created or converted into a signup record once we're able to map uh the raw / Kobi Kunasekaran: data to the right deal right deal rep association
items.note: Restatement of the process in an internal walkthrough; no client attendee.

items.topic: Sign-up complete after proofs and dates
items.statement: The rep or brand ambassador enters proofs, sign-up date, deposit amount and any referral; when the three proofs and dates are complete the sign-up is complete and a payout to the player follows.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: The rep or brand ambassador would enter this information in. And once all the information, like everything that's necessary for a deal, like the three proofs and the dates and everything is done, a signup is considered complete. And then once that's complete, they would pay out like a commission uh or like an additional bonus to the player that signed up.
items.note: Restatement of the process in an internal walkthrough; no client attendee.

items.topic: Link cap tracking and auto-deactivation deferred
items.statement: No link expiry or cap tracking is built today. The first phase moves tracking from spreadsheets into Salesforce for reporting; tracking assignment counts and deactivating links in Salesforce is a possible future state.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: Uh I've seen uh I've seen that um it seems that the link can be used for um x amount of time. Do we already uh do we have a tracker for that? Uh does that link automatically expires / Kobi Kunasekaran: we don't have anything like that uh built in right now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So really the first phase is let's let's get all of that out and by virtue of putting in Salesforce we already have the relationships and everything so we can get that reporting and then in a future state there's nothing stopping us from um you know tracking how many assignments are done and deactivating the link directly here right so that's probably what we'll work towards
items.note: Jumpr-internal direction; not confirmed with the client in this meeting.

items.topic: Lean MVP scope; extras need client buy-in
items.statement: Jumpr keeps the scope lean as an MVP that replaces spreadsheets, avoids over-engineering, and needs client buy-in for anything extra.
items.quote: Cedrick Infantado: So it seems that uh it is just an MVP moving away from the spreadsheet and just going to sales. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Exactly. Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So again, try to keep it simple, keep the scope lean, and then for anything extra, we got to like get buy in, right?
items.note: Jumpr-internal delivery posture. A related commercial remark on line 294 was skipped under rule 5.

items.topic: Draft homepage not yet shown
items.statement: Kobi built a draft homepage that shows information in one place for sales reps/brand ambassadors and ops; it is not yet shown to the client and needs cleanup.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I even like tried like set set up this like homepage. page. I haven't shown them this yet. Um because I think it still needs work. Like there's a lot of field gear and everything I want to clean up, but like a place where they can see all the information uh from one place and like the visa records and stuff for both like sales reps or the brand ambassadors and ops.
items.asr_note: 'visa records' may be an ASR error (unclear term)

items.topic: User stories from link mockup feedback
items.statement: Karen is writing user stories from the previous day's feedback session on the client's link mockups; until an API endpoint exists, little can be set up on the Salesforce side for the integration.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Karen's working on putting together the user stories based on our feedback session from yesterday for things like this. like this is all like actually the mockup that we walked through yesterday in the two call. So if there are any stories that we could pick up until because I feel like at this point until we have a API endpoint there's not much we can do uh to set up anything on the Salesforce side.

items.topic: Assign link screen flows before API work
items.statement: If API endpoints are not available by this week, Kobi will assign Cedrick stories such as screen flows for creating links and modals from the client mockups; Apex integration work starts once endpoints exist.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: some stories that I can assign uh over to you to work on that might be like you know screen flows for creating the the links like they've mocked up here / Kobi Kunasekaran: organization familiar with the uh with the data object model and everything um and then once we have the gun points we can start the uh apex work that we need to / Kobi Kunasekaran: So after parent puts together the user stories like if we don't have the API endpoints and stuff by like this week then uh what I'll do is like I'll uh I'll we'll pivot let's I'll assign some of the stories over to you for you know like the modals and things like that screen flows and stuff / Cedrick Infantado: Okay, sure.
items.due: Conditional: if no API endpoints by end of this week (week of 2026-08-17)

items.topic: Prototype in Salesforce instead of mockups
items.statement: Jumpr built the first design from the PRD and discovery directly in Salesforce, and told the client it is faster to configure in Salesforce and take feedback than to produce mockup cycles; some PRD fields were later not needed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: because she did the the did the PRD with, um, with Cloud as well, like there was a lot of field that we added that they actually didn't end up needing. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So that's what like we told them like look like we can spend the time but we're just going to be burning hours. It's faster for us to do it straight in Salesforce and then we can show you and you can give us feedback and we'll we can make adjustments from there.
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee. Client acceptance of this approach is not stated in this doc.

items.topic: Mid-August UAT and go-live dropped
items.statement: Kobi says the earlier target of mid-August UAT and go-live was moved away from; no new date is stated.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and this was actually in anticipation of a mid August uh UAT uh and go live but we moved away from that.
items.supersedes_hint: Earlier plan: mid-August UAT and go-live. Now: moved away from that; no replacement date stated.
items.note: Rest of line 438 is personnel content and was not recorded (rule 5).

items.topic: API spec is Jumpr proposal only
items.statement: The API spec document is a Jumpr-proposed design; the client has given no requirements or API endpoints, and the design will change based on how the client builds its CMS.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: in the uh API spec document that I shared u again that's like a proposed design right like that I put that together based on how we would approach the uh the implementation or the integration, but we don't have any part requirements from their end. We don't have any uh API endpoints to work off of or anything like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, uh it's going to change based on how they build their CMS. So, just keep that in mind like nothing is set in stone.

items.topic: Client approvals; storage proofs and CMS go-ahead
items.statement: For WagerTech, approvals are generally enough to start work (no signed document). Kobi says the client gave a thumbs up on the storage proofs and CMS integration estimate documents, so Jumpr proceeds as if both go forward.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, generally just approvals are enough. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, But obviously larger projects like for the storage proofs and even the CMS integration [...] So they've given us a thumbs up um so we proceed as if you know we're going to go forward with it.
items.note: Secondhand: Kobi reports the client position in a Jumpr-internal standup; no client attendee. Commercial wording on lines 458 and 463 elided under rule 5 ([...] marks the elision; no words changed).
